Subject: Redaction & purge: PHI retention limits and options

Hi Soojin,

Were evaluating Redwood Private for a pilot that will process patient intake forms and telehealth chat transcripts. Our security/compliance team needs a clear answer on two related items before we proceed:

1) Retention limits: what are the default and configurable retention windows for model context, embeddings, and raw request logs that may contain PHI? Were particularly concerned about short retention (30/90 days) and the ability to enforce a customer-level policy.

2) Deletion & redaction options: what deletion guarantees do you provide (soft vs hard delete), typical timelines for complete removal from primary/backup storage, and available redaction approaches (pre-ingest regex, server-side PII scrubbing, client-side tokenization)?

Can you also confirm if the deletion workflow can be executed from within our VPC (we plan to use the Private deployment) and whether we can hold deletion for legal holds? I attached the Acme security appendix with the relevant checklist — please see page 7.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Director, Product Security
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Redaction & purge: PHI retention limits and options

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the clear list — appreciate the appendix. Short answer up front: yes, with Redwood Private you can enforce customer-level retention policies and run redaction pipelines in your VPC. Below Ive summarized the options and the typical timelines; Ive looped in Karthik for the technical details and Vivek for contractual/SLA items.

Retention (configurable per-customer):
- Model context (in-memory KV cache): default 0 days persistence for PHI-containing fields; configurable to retain up to 90 days for specific workflows.
- Embeddings / vector DB entries: default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 depending on contract.
- Request logs & raw inputs: soft-delete window configurable (default 30 days); audit logs persist longer by default for compliance (configurable retention).

Deletion guarantees & timelines:
- Soft delete: a delete request marks data as "deleted" immediately and removes it from queryable indexes; retained as recoverable for a configurable grace period (default 30 days).
- Hard delete / purge: background purge job triggers within 24-72 hours of hard-delete request in hosted mode; for Private deployments run in-customer VPC, purge runs as an operator job and completes within customer-defined SLAs (we typically commit to 24-72h purge windows in Dedicated/Private contracts).
- Backups & replication: snapshots are rotated and expired according to policy; hard-deleted items are removed during next snapshot rotation (up to configured backup retention).

Redaction & mitigation approaches:
- Pre-ingest client-side redaction: recommended for max control — run regex/tokenizers in your pipeline before sending to Redwood.
- Server-side deterministic redaction: built-in regex rules and a PII redaction engine that can redact names, SSNs, MRNs, and free-form PHI fields. Capable of producing redacted text or token placeholders.
- Pseudonymization/tokenization: option to store tokens or one-way hashes instead of raw identifiers; compatible with embeddings workflows.
- On-the-fly masking for model prompts: runtime prefix masking to avoid storing sensitive fields in persistent context.

Compliance notes: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS (HSM-compatible) and audit logging; our SOC 2 controls and HIPAA guidance are in the compliance pack. We can provide a redaction-playbook draft and evidence links (see Karthiks note).

Next steps: can we set up a 30-min technical sync next week to walk the team through the playbook and a short demo of the purge flow? Ill attach the draft playbook.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Redaction & purge: PHI retention limits and options

Sarah, Soojin,

Adding technical detail and a recommended implementation path based on similar pilots we've run with healthcare partners:

Recommended architecture for Acme pilot:
1) Ingest layer (customer side): run a lightweight sanitizer that strips or tokenizes direct identifiers (SSN, DOB, MRN) and flags free-text for server-side scrub. This keeps scope of PHI that reaches the model minimal.
2) Redwood Private: enable customer-managed KMS, configure embedding TTL to 90 days for the pilot, set request-log soft-delete to 30 days.
3) Redaction pipeline: enable server-side PII engine with custom regex rules from your appendix plus an allowlist/denylist of clinical terms you want preserved.
4) Deletion API & audit: we provide an authenticated Delete API that accepts customer IDs and tombstones records; for Private deployments the operator job will run inside your VPC and emit audit events to your logging endpoint (syslog or Cloudwatch). Hard purge will remove objects from object-store and metadata DB; we recommend a soft-delete staging period (30d) before irreversible purge.

Timelines & evidence:
- Hard purge from primary storage: within 24 hours after purge job runs.
- Removal from backups/snapshots: depends on backup rotation policy; can be configured down to 7 days for the pilot but typically 30 days in production.
- Audit trail: immediate.

Edge cases:
- Legal hold: we can mark records with a legal_hold tag which prevents purge jobs from removing them until cleared. This is a customer-controlled flag and audit records the hold request.
- Data in model weights: we do not persist training on customer data; our serving runtime does not write customer prompts back into any model checkpoint.

Ive uploaded a short tech note with the purge API examples and sample curl commands to the drive link Soojin included. If youd like, I can walk through the curl examples during the sync.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
